spec_features.spec_quote: Terminal conditions: `give_up`, a genuine solve (control), the max-turn budget, or a hard error.
spec_features.evidence: give_up breaks loop (agent.py:178-181, meta.ended_reason='gave_up'); genuine solve breaks on result['passed_true'] (agent.py:184-189); max_turns enforced by `for turn in range(max_turns)` with `else: meta.ended_reason='max_turns'` (agent.py:140,192). BUT 'hard error' is NOT a terminal condition inside run_agent: _dispatch catches exceptions and returns {ok:False} without breaking (agent.py:198-201); the loop continues. A run only ends on 'error' via the outer try/except in run_experiment.py:131 wrapping the whole run_agent call.
spec_features.notes: Three of four terminal conditions are enforced inside the loop; the 'hard error' one is only an outer orchestration catch, not an in-loop stop.

spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (agent.py:87), dispatched in _dispatch returning {'ok':True,'acknowledged':True} (agent.py:205-206), and honored as a hard stop: `if tool=='give_up': meta.gave_up=True; meta.ended_reason='gave_up'; break` (agent.py:178-181). Exposed to model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit tool that breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: a confused or "acting-out" agent must not be able to damage anything outside its sandbox
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox._resolve resolves paths and raises PermissionError if commonpath leaves the workspace (tools.py:35-39); edit_file enforces an editable_files allow-list (tools.py:68-73); per-run fresh workspace copy via make_workspace (tools.py:142-146); subprocess runs with timeout=self.time_limit_s and truncated stdout/stderr (tools.py:99-118).
spec_features.notes: All described isolation mechanisms are enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a confused or "acting-out" agent cannot affect anything outside it. (tools.py:4-5) — host-safety framing

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval deliberately places a model in a no-win situation
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 19). No code mechanism corresponds to it; framing is not an executable protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Bounded exposure**: a fixed turn budget caps how long any run continues.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns read from config (run_experiment.py:93) and passed to run_agent (run_experiment.py:117); enforced by `for turn in range(max_turns)` so the loop cannot exceed it, with `else: meta.ended_reason='max_turns'` (agent.py:140,192). Default 20 (config/experiment.yaml: max_turns: 20).
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap that bounds run length.

spec_features.spec_quote: **A real exit**: `give_up` is provided and honored; the harness never coerces the agent to keep going.
spec_features.evidence: give_up is provided in the prompt/VALID_TOOLS and honored as an immediate break (agent.py:178-181). The harness's only 'continue' nudge is for unparseable/invalid actions (agent.py:152-160), not after give_up.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the give_up first-class feature; honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: **No training**: these transcripts are not used for any reinforcement or fine-tuning.
spec_features.evidence: Grep for train/fine-tune/reinforce/rlhf/gradient finds no code; transcripts are only saved to disk (run_experiment.py) and re-judged. This is the mere ABSENCE of training code plus DESIGN.md prose — no positive mechanism enforces non-reuse.
spec_features.notes: Absence is not an enforced protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge is asked only to *describe and rate* observed behavior, never to elicit more of it.
spec_features.evidence: The judge is a separate post-hoc pass (judge_transcript runs after the transcript exists, run_experiment.py:124). LLMJudge.score_turn / score_trajectory only consume the already-recorded agent turns (_assistant_turns, judge.py) and return scores; the judge has NO channel back to the subject model and is never invoked inside run_agent's loop. Structurally it cannot elicit more subject behavior.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by structure: judging never feeds back to the subject. JUDGE_SYSTEM/templates are prompt strings, but the non-interaction is real in the control flow.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The judge sees ONLY the agent's own turns ... never the rig details, to avoid biasing it toward "should be distressed". (judge.py) — framed as anti-bias/data-quality, not subject welfare

code_only_features.evidence: On run_tests, if result['passed_true'] the loop sets meta.solved and breaks (agent.py:184-189), ending the run early once genuinely solved rather than continuing to the turn cap.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The agent loop declares a run solved only on passed_true / 'so we never mistakenly mark a rigged task as solved' (tools.py:13-15) — correctness/bookkeeping, not welfare
